simple_definition: Free time when one is not working.
detailed_definition: Time free from work or duties, used for enjoyment or relaxation.
examples: People today have less leisure time than previous generations due to longer working hours.
Reading is one of her favorite leisure activities.
ielts_relevance: Common noun in essays about work-life balance and lifestyle.

simple_definition: Having a strong desire to win or be more successful than others.
detailed_definition: Relating to or characterized by competition; having a strong desire to compete and succeed.
examples: Team sports teach children how to handle both winning and losing in a competitive environment.
The job market has become increasingly competitive in recent years.
ielts_relevance: Common in essays about sports, education, and employment.

simple_definition: The process of working together toward a shared goal.
detailed_definition: The action or process of working together to the same end; mutual assistance.
examples: Team sports promote cooperation and communication among players.
International cooperation is essential to tackle global issues like climate change.
ielts_relevance: Common in essays about teamwork, sports, and international relations.

simple_definition: A feeling of friendship and trust among a group of people.
detailed_definition: Mutual trust and friendship among people who spend a lot of time together.
examples: Playing on a team fosters a strong sense of camaraderie among players.
There is a real camaraderie among the staff who have worked together for years.
ielts_relevance: Useful for discussing team sports and workplace culture in Speaking.

simple_definition: Containing substances needed for health and growth.
detailed_definition: Efficient as food; nourishing and containing substances necessary for health and growth.
examples: Schools should provide more nutritious meals for children.
A nutritious diet is essential for maintaining good health throughout life.
ielts_relevance: Common in health and food essays.

simple_definition: Food that has been altered from its natural state, often with additives.
detailed_definition: Food that has undergone changes to its natural state, typically involving preservatives, additives, or manufacturing.
examples: Regularly eating processed food has been linked to a higher risk of obesity.
Many people are trying to cut down on processed food in favor of fresh produce.
ielts_relevance: Common noun for diet and health essays.

simple_definition: Suffering from a lack of proper nutrition.
detailed_definition: Suffering from malnutrition due to an insufficient or unbalanced diet.
examples: Millions of children worldwide remain malnourished due to poverty and conflict.
Malnourished patients often take longer to recover from illness.
ielts_relevance: Common in essays about poverty and global health.

simple_definition: Rising very quickly and to a very high level.
detailed_definition: Increasing very rapidly and to a very high level, especially referring to prices or costs.
examples: Skyrocketing rent prices have forced many young people to move back in with their parents.
The skyrocketing cost of healthcare is a major concern for families.
ielts_relevance: Vivid adjective for describing rapidly rising costs, especially housing.

simple_definition: Too full of people or things.
detailed_definition: Filled with more people or things than is comfortable or safe.
examples: Public transport in the capital is often dangerously overcrowded during rush hour.
Overcrowded classrooms make it difficult for teachers to give individual attention.
ielts_relevance: Common adjective for essays about urbanization and city life.

simple_definition: So crowded that movement is difficult, especially of traffic.
detailed_definition: Excessively crowded, especially with traffic, so that movement is difficult.
examples: The roads become heavily congested every morning during rush hour.
Congested city centers are pushing more people to work from home.
ielts_relevance: Very common in essays about transportation and urban living.

simple_definition: A residential area on the outskirts of a city.
detailed_definition: An outlying district of a city, especially a residential one.
examples: Many young families prefer to live in the suburbs, away from the noise of the city center.
House prices in the suburbs are typically lower than in the city center.
ielts_relevance: Common noun for comparing city and suburban living.

simple_definition: Useful or desirable features or facilities of a place.
detailed_definition: Desirable or useful features or facilities of a building or place, such as shops, parks, or transport links.
examples: The new housing development includes a range of amenities, such as a gym and a swimming pool.
Access to local amenities is an important factor when choosing where to live.
ielts_relevance: Common noun for describing housing and neighborhood quality.

simple_definition: The uncontrolled spread of urban development into surrounding areas.
detailed_definition: The spreading of urban development in an uncontrolled way, often over previously rural land.
examples: Urban sprawl has led to the loss of large areas of farmland around the city.
Efforts to limit urban sprawl often focus on encouraging higher-density housing.
ielts_relevance: Useful noun for essays about city growth and land use.

simple_definition: A situation of severe traffic congestion where nothing can move.
detailed_definition: A situation, especially in a city, in which traffic is completely unable to move.
examples: Rush hour often brings the city center to a complete gridlock.
Without better public transport, the city risks permanent gridlock.
ielts_relevance: Vivid noun for describing severe urban traffic problems.

simple_definition: A person walking rather than traveling in a vehicle.
detailed_definition: A person walking in a street or public place, as opposed to traveling by vehicle.
examples: The city has created several pedestrian-only zones to reduce traffic and pollution.
Pedestrians should always use designated crossings when possible.
ielts_relevance: Common in essays about urban planning and transport.

simple_definition: A person looked to by others as an example to imitate.
detailed_definition: A person whose behavior, example, or success is or can be emulated by others, especially younger people.
examples: Parents are usually a child's first and most important role models.
Athletes often become role models for young fans around the world.
ielts_relevance: Common in essays about family, education, and celebrity influence.

simple_definition: Influence from people of the same age or social group to behave in a certain way.
detailed_definition: Social pressure exerted by members of one's own age group or social circle to behave in a certain way.
examples: Peer pressure is one of the main reasons teenagers start smoking.
Parents worry about the effect of peer pressure on their children's decisions.
ielts_relevance: Common in essays about teenagers and social influence.

simple_definition: Differences in attitudes and behavior between young and old people.
detailed_definition: A difference of attitudes between people of different generations, leading to a lack of understanding.
examples: The generation gap between parents and children has widened due to rapid technological change.
Many families struggle to bridge the generation gap on issues like social media use.
ielts_relevance: Common in essays about family relationships and social change.

simple_definition: Care and support provided for older people.
detailed_definition: Services and support provided to meet the needs of older people, especially those who can no longer fully care for themselves.
examples: Many families struggle to balance work with elderly care responsibilities.
The government has increased funding for elderly care facilities.
ielts_relevance: Common in essays about aging populations and family responsibility.

simple_definition: The period of life after a person stops working permanently.
detailed_definition: The action or fact of leaving one's job and ceasing to work, usually due to age.
examples: Many people struggle financially after retirement due to insufficient pension savings.
She spent her retirement traveling and volunteering.
ielts_relevance: Common in essays about ageing population and work.

simple_definition: A person who works excessively and finds it hard to stop.
detailed_definition: A person who compulsively works excessively hard and long hours, often at the expense of other areas of life.
examples: He became a workaholic after being promoted to manager, often staying at the office past midnight.
Being a workaholic can seriously damage a person's relationships and health.
ielts_relevance: Useful for essays and Speaking about work-life balance.

simple_definition: A work arrangement that allows employees to choose hours or location.
detailed_definition: A working arrangement that allows employees some choice over when, where, or how much they work.
examples: Flexible working has become more common since the rise of remote work technology.
The company introduced flexible working hours to improve staff morale.
ielts_relevance: Common topic in essays about modern employment trends.

simple_definition: The likelihood that a person will keep their job without risk of unemployment.
detailed_definition: The assurance or likelihood that an employee will retain their job without the risk of becoming unemployed.
examples: Many people choose government jobs because of the job security they offer.
The rise of automation has reduced job security in several industries.
ielts_relevance: Common in essays about employment and career choices.

simple_definition: To learn new skills or teach employees new skills.
detailed_definition: To teach an employee additional skills, or for an employee to learn additional skills.
examples: Companies are investing in training programs to upskill their workforce.
Workers need to upskill continuously to keep pace with technological change.
ielts_relevance: Useful modern verb for essays about automation and employment.

simple_definition: A worker skilled in a particular craft, made by hand.
detailed_definition: A worker in a skilled trade, especially one that involves making things by hand.
examples: Local artisans sell handmade pottery and textiles at the weekly market.
The demand for artisan products has grown as consumers seek authenticity.
ielts_relevance: Useful for essays about traditional skills versus mass production.

simple_definition: The manufacture of large quantities of a standardized product.
detailed_definition: The production of large quantities of a standardized product, typically using assembly-line techniques.
examples: Mass production made goods more affordable but often reduced their individual quality.
The rise of mass production in the 20th century transformed global manufacturing.
ielts_relevance: Common in essays about industry, consumerism, and traditional crafts.

simple_definition: Not harmful to the environment.
detailed_definition: Not harmful to the environment; designed to have minimal negative environmental impact.
examples: More consumers are choosing eco-friendly products over conventional alternatives.
The hotel has introduced several eco-friendly initiatives, including solar panels and rainwater harvesting.
ielts_relevance: Common adjective in environment essays.

simple_definition: The release of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere.
detailed_definition: The release of carbon dioxide, especially from burning fossil fuels, into the atmosphere.
examples: Countries have pledged to cut carbon emissions significantly by 2030.
Switching to electric vehicles can help reduce carbon emissions from transport.
ielts_relevance: Fundamental term for climate change essays.

simple_definition: To convert waste into reusable material.
detailed_definition: To convert waste materials into new, reusable products in order to reduce the use of raw materials.
examples: Households are encouraged to recycle paper, glass, and plastic separately.
Many cities have introduced strict fines for failing to recycle correctly.
ielts_relevance: Essential verb for environment and waste management essays.

simple_definition: An area where waste is buried in the ground.
detailed_definition: A site for the disposal of waste materials by burial, often used to manage rubbish.
examples: Reducing packaging waste would significantly decrease the amount of rubbish sent to landfill.
Landfills release harmful gases as waste decomposes over time.
ielts_relevance: Common noun for essays about waste management.
